name: Evergy
tagline: Delivering affordable, reliable and sustainable electricity to Kansas and Missouri
hero_kpi_rationale: Evergy prévoit investir 21,6 milliards de dollars d'ici 2030, incluant 9,3 milliards en nouvelles capacités de génération (gaz naturel, énergies renouvelables et stockage par batterie) pour soutenir la croissance économique et moderniser son infrastructure dans le Kansas et le Missouri.

kpis.signal: Plan capex releve chaque annee, moteur central de la croissance du benefice regule.

kpis.short: Large customer electric service agreements signed
kpis.signal: Compte cumulatif des contrats data centers/grande charge, cle de la strategie de croissance.
Base clientele Kansas/Missouri, stable autour de 1,7 million.

kpis.name_fr: Croissance de la demande normalisee du climat
kpis.signal: Croissance sous-jacente des ventes hors effet meteo, en acceleration avec les grandes charges.

kpis.name_fr: Pointe de charge contractee des grands clients
kpis.signal: Les cinq contrats data centers plus Panasonic totalisent 3 GW de pointe (2,5 GW LLPS + 450 MW non-LLPS), soit +600 MW en un trimestre.

kpis.name_fr: Croissance annuelle de la charge de detail jusqu'en 2030
kpis.signal: Prevision de croissance de la charge relevee a 7-8% par an jusqu'en 2030, contre 6% auparavant, portee par les grands clients.

kpis.short: Nuclear production tax credits flowed back to Kansas customers
kpis.name_fr: Credits d'impot nucleaires reverses aux clients Kansas
kpis.signal: Accord unanime approuve par la KCC pour reverser plus de 100 M$/an de credits d'impot nucleaires aux clients sur trois ans.
Tarifs globaux seulement 5,1% plus eleves qu'en 2017, soit bien moins de 1% par an, tres en dessous de l'inflation.
Pipeline d'opportunites grands clients de plus de 15 GW, l'un des carnets les plus robustes du pays rapporte a la taille de la societe.
La centrale nucleaire Wolf Creek produit environ 1 200 MW d'energie sans carbone, de quoi alimenter plus de 800 000 foyers.
Hausse de 4% du dividende trimestriel a 2,78$ par action annualise, visant le milieu de la fourchette de distribution 60-70%.
Cible d'economies d'O&M portee a 345 M$ par an d'ici 2025 depuis la base 2018, soit une reduction de plus de 25%.

kpis.short: Winter storm Uri securitization Missouri West
kpis.name_fr: Titrisation des couts tempete Uri Missouri West
kpis.signal: Demande de titrisation d'environ 295 M$ de surcouts de la tempete hivernale Uri au Missouri West, recuperes sur quinze ans pour lisser l'impact client.

Construction de deux centrales gaz a cycle combine au Kansas d'environ 705 MW chacune (1 410 MW au total), en service au printemps 2029 et 2030, co-detenues par Evergy Kansas Central et Evergy Missouri West.
Evergy Missouri West prevoit une centrale gaz a cycle simple de 440 MW dans le Missouri, mise en service attendue en 2030.
Les Evergy Companies disposent d'environ 15 800 MW de capacite de production detenue et d'achats d'energie renouvelable pour desservir 1,7 million de clients au Kansas et Missouri.
Evergy Kansas Central developpe la centrale solaire Kansas Sky de 159 MW dans le comte de Douglas (Kansas), calendrier de mise en service incertain en raison d'un litige.
En janvier-fevrier 2026 Evergy a rachete 244,1 M$ de principal de ses obligations convertibles 4,50% pour un cout total de 308,6 M$, ramenant l'encours a 1 155,9 M$.

ai_positioning.summary: While not explicitly mentioned in MD&A, Evergy's signed data center agreements (1,900 MW of new large load) in February 2026 implicitly position the company to benefit from AI infrastructure demand and computational workload growth in its service territories.
evidence: 1,900 MW of new large load agreements signed with data centers (Feb 2026)
LLPS rate plans approved to support large load customers
Strategic focus on economic development and new business attraction
ai_positioning.source: MD&A - Large Load Power Service Rate Plans section, 10-K 2025

risks.title: Regulatory Risk
risks.score_rationale: Missouri SB 4 (2025) and Kansas HB 2107 (2025) established new regulatory mechanisms and compliance requirements affecting cost recovery and generation planning for natural gas and renewable assets.
risks.summary: Regulatory changes in Missouri and Kansas affect construction cost recovery mechanisms (CWIP), PISA provisions, and generation asset classifications through 2035.

risks.title: Capital Investment Risk
risks.score_rationale: Execution risk on $21.6 billion capex plan through 2030, including $9.3 billion in new generation capacity requiring technology deployment and project completion.
risks.summary: Large-scale infrastructure investment programs involve execution, cost overrun, and commodity price risks.

risks.title: Debt and Financing Risk
risks.score_rationale: Significant capital expenditure plans require access to debt and equity capital markets at favorable terms to maintain financial stability and investment-grade ratings.
risks.summary: Dependence on capital markets for $21.6 billion investment program creates refinancing and interest rate exposure.

risks.title: Competitive Demand Risk
risks.score_rationale: Large load customer agreements (1,900 MW data center load) expose utility to customer concentration risk and competitive pressure from alternative power suppliers.
risks.summary: Increasing competition for large load customers in regional power markets may affect contract renewal and rate negotiations.

risks.title: Environmental and Catastrophic Risk
risks.score_rationale: Extreme weather events, natural disasters and climate impacts on transmission/distribution infrastructure in Kansas and Missouri service territories.
risks.summary: Operational disruptions from severe weather, grid outages, and infrastructure damage could impact reliability metrics and customer service.

risks.title: Generation Portfolio Transition Risk
risks.score_rationale: Transition from traditional coal generation to natural gas, renewables and battery storage requires technology integration, supply chain reliability and grid modernization.
risks.summary: Modernization of generation fleet creates technology and operational risks during transition period.

risks.title: Tax and Policy Risk
risks.score_rationale: Federal Omnibus Budget and Business Advancement Act (OBBBA, July 2025) modified clean energy production tax credits affecting long-term renewable generation planning assumptions.
risks.summary: Changes in federal tax incentives for clean energy may impact economic returns on renewable generation investments.

governance.voting_structure: Une seule classe d'actions ordinaires, 1 vote par action.

comp_detail.perf_metrics_bonus: Prime annuelle liee a la performance financiere (BPA ajuste et benefices ajustes) et a des objectifs operationnels, avec un paiement pondere de 95,5% de la cible pour 2025.

company_description: Evergy, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, engages in the generation, transmission, distribution, and sale of electricity in the United States. The company generates electricity through coal, landfill gas, uranium, and natural gas and oil sources, as well as solar, wind, and other renewable sources. It serves residences, commercial firms, industrials, municipalities, and other electric utilities. The company was incorporated in 2017 and is headquartered in Kansas City, Missouri.
